title: Critical Review of Six Epistemic Dimensions of Social Media Audio
paragraphs:
Chapter 2
Critical Review of Six Epistemic Dimensions
of Social Media Audio
Chapter abstract. This chapter reviews six epistemic dimensions of social-media
audio: the manufacture of consent, the architecture of attention, the velocity of un-
truth, the parasocial epistemic bond, the measurement of the mind, and the student
as epistemic agent. It assesses what communication research, platform studies, and
measurement theory can support, and it identies rival explanations.
The review
motivates EST and the LOKLOK design while agging the gaps: platform-specic
evidence, longitudinal outcomes, and validated student measures.
This chapter reviews the literature that motivates Epistemic Systems The-
ory (EST). The review is organised along six dimensions, each of which identies
a mechanism that shapes what users believe and how they judge information: the
manufacture of consent, the architecture of attention, the velocity of untruth, the
parasocial epistemic bond, the measurement of the mind, and the student as epis-
temic agent. The purpose of the review is not exhaustiveness but theoretical ground-
ing: each dimension contributes a distinct constraint that EST must accommodate,
and each is revisited when the framework is developed in Chapter 3.
16

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
17
2.1
Review Scope and Appraisal Criteria
The review is a critical narrative synthesis. Sources were selected for relevance to
audio distribution, audience judgment, platform mechanisms, measurement, and
the Egyptian setting. The expansion includes targeted publisher and institutional
searches for radiosocial-network relations,
podcast platformisation,
listening
context, algorithm experiments, and measurement reporting. It includes research
published through 2026; no exhaustive search, formal quality-scoring exercise, or
systematic-review registration is claimed.
Each study is appraised by its object, research design, population, outcome,
main contribution, and limits of transfer to this thesis. Abstract-only information is
not represented as full-text appraisal. In particular, the Egyptian study is discussed
at the scope supported by its published abstract. Journal prestige or sample size
alone does not determine relevance: a large study of text feeds need not measure the
same process as an audio-listening study. Evidence about architecture, exposure,
evaluation, and learning is kept separate throughout.
The main currency window is publication years 20162026, through the re-
vision date of September 8, 2026. Older sources are retained for original concepts
and authoritative methods, including Shannon's entropy, Cronbach's alpha, Horton
and Wohl's parasocial concept, DeGroot's opinion model, Herman and Chomsky's
propaganda framework, and the 2014 testing standards. The statistical explanation
also cites foundational association and Bayesian methods. Recent research supplies
criticism and application rather than allowing these classics to stand in for current

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
18
evidence. One agent-simulation source is explicitly labelled a preprint.
2.2
Radio, Platforms, and Social Participation
Spinelli and Dann (2019) examine podcasting as an audio medium with distinctive
production practices and relationships between producers and listeners. Its value
for EST is a shift in the unit of explanation: public interaction extends beyond the
broadcast. Its limitation is equally important: identifying new relationships does
not estimate an interface's eect on credibility. Participation can be invited without
being realised, and visible comments need not represent silent listeners.
Sullivan (2019) examines podcast platformisation through infrastructure and
industry organisation. His storagediscoveryconsumption distinction helps locate
where a platform acquires inuence over audio.
An industry analysis, however,
is not a randomised audience study. For EST, a gatekeeping claim must identify
the selection rule and its consequence, rather than infer persuasion directly from
ownership or concentration.
Rime et al. (2022) characterise podcasting through multiple tensions and
innovations, cautioning against dening it through one delivery technology. The
present thesis consequently distinguishes a streamed programme, a social post, and
an on-demand episode. This conceptual work claries the object of study; it does
not demonstrate a particular LOKLOK mechanism.
Groot Kormelink et al. (2025) asked 60 participants to listen to a daily news
podcast for up to four weeks and interviewed them afterward. The study highlights
the importance of tting listening into specic routines.
Its instructed listening

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
19
arrangement supplies contextual depth but diers from an unprompted population
survey. It motivates examining reception context; it does not establish that longer
rides cause higher PB scores in Giza.
2.3
Egyptian Audience Research and Contextual Transfer
Wajih and Al-Yamani (2024) investigate Egyptian young people's use of podcast
applications for political and economic issues. Their published abstract describes an
online questionnaire with a purposive sample of 400 users and an interest in interac-
tion, content evaluation, and trust. The study adopts a public-sphere perspective.
This is a characteristic of the reviewed study, not a replacement for EST in the
present thesis.
This research prevents a claim that Egyptian audio-audience scholarship is
absent. Its purposive sample does not establish national prevalence, and its broad
podcast population diers from university students listening during journeys. The
comparison concerns questions and context, not a numerical replication. No unre-
ported coecients from that study enter this analysis.
Contextual transfer requires more than translating a questionnaire. Language
variety, host familiarity, topic sensitivity, shared-device listening, and relationships
among vehicle occupants could inuence responses. These are conditions to inves-
tigate, not explanations already measured here. Institution labels and the journey
setting do not establish respondents' socioeconomic position, political views, or at-
tention.

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
20
2.4
What Algorithm Research Supportsand What It Does
Not
Lorenz-Spreen et al. (2023) systematically review causal and correlational evidence
on digital media and democracy. Their synthesis identies patterns that dier by
outcome and context, rather than a uniform relationship. The lesson for EST is
to specify both the outcome and the design that identies it. Participation, trust,
knowledge, and polarisation are not interchangeable measures of one platform eect.
Gauthier et al. (2026) report a seven-week experiment conducted on X in
2023. Switching from a chronological to an algorithmic feed shifted some political
opinions; switching in the opposite direction produced no comparable eect. Neither
manipulation signicantly changed aective polarisation or self-reported partisan-
ship. This supports taking architecture seriously while rejecting an automatic infer-
ence from a feed change to every attitude. Its ndings concern a platform, period,
and active-user population, not radio listeners or LOKLOK.
For EST-P1, the bounded proposition is that a specied architectural change
may alter a specied outcome under dened conditions. Neither study proves that
architecture always outweighs user characteristics. Prior exposure and user choices
can modify an intervention's eect: a platform can inuence whom someone fol-
lows, while those following choices subsequently inuence what the platform delivers.
Structural inuence and user agency need not be mutually exclusive explanations.

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
21
2.5
Propagation, Correction, and Audience Judgment
Pennycook et al. (2021) distinguish judgments of headline accuracy from sharing
intentions and report experiments in which directing attention to accuracy improved
the quality of subsequent sharing. Pennycook and Rand (2022) extend this evidence
through an internal meta-analysis of 20 experiments. Consistency across those ex-
periments is informative, but the internal scope and frequent use of headline-sharing
tasks limit direct transfer to audio. Neither paper validates the BRS or an audio-
transcript classier.
Ecker et al. (2022) review cognitive, social, and aective inuences on misin-
formation belief and correction, including continued inuence after correction. This
makes correction a process rather than a binary platform action. Publishing, deliver-
ing, noticing, accepting, and later using a correction are distinct events. A platform
cannot infer the last stage merely because it logged the rst.
These distinctions make EST more testable. If a badge changes PB but not
accuracy discernment, the nding concerns a credibility cue. If a prompt changes
sharing but not belief, it concerns behaviour rather than persuasion.
If source
diversity increases alongside the circulation of inaccurate sources, diversity alone has
not established better information. These are competing outcomes, not inconvenient
cases to exclude from evaluation.

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
22
2.6
Measurement Debate Rather Than Coecient Counting
McNeish (2018) argues for closer attention to reliability assumptions and alternatives
to routinely reporting alpha.
Raykov and Marcoulides (2019) counter a blanket
rejection: alpha remains useful when its relationship to score reliability is justied by
the measurement conditions. The disagreement does not license selecting whichever
coecient is largest. It requires specifying the score, model, and inferential purpose.
The balanced position here is to preserve the reported coecients, disclose
factor-t problems, and avoid turning either alpha or an unspecied omega into a
validity certicate. A reliable score can measure the wrong construct, and a plausi-
ble construct name does not establish equivalent measurement across languages or
institutions. EST-P3 is an accountability requirement precisely because it permits
an unfavourable measurement result.
2.7
The Manufacture of Consent
Herman and Chomsky's propaganda model (1988) argued that mass media sys-
tematically lter which claims become visible: ownership and advertising interests,
sourcing routines, ak, and ideology jointly shape the content that reaches audi-
ences. The model anticipated the modern insight that what users see is not what
is true but what institutional lters admit. Its relevance to social media audio is
direct: algorithmic platforms inherited the ltering role of mass media but execute
it with a metric now visible to users and amenable to scientic measurement.
Chomsky's paradigm anchors EST-P1, the proposition that the architecture

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
23
of a media system, not the psychology of individual consumers, is the primary
determinant of the epistemic output. A social media radio platform whose ranking
function rewards engagement will amplify a dierent distribution of claims than one
whose ranking function rewards veried diversity, regardless of the qualities of the
audience. The propaganda model supplies the intellectual precedent for treating the
lter itself as the unit of analysis.
2.8
The Architecture of Attention
Wu (2016) traced the attention merchants who have, since the nineteenth cen-
tury, harvested human attention and sold it. Zubo (2019) extended the analysis
to surveillance capitalism, in which behavioural surplus is extracted from users and
converted into prediction products. On social media, the attention architecture is
executed by recommender systems whose optimisation targets are set by the plat-
form. Gillespie (2018) documented how content moderation, the custodians of the
internet, quietly shapes the public sphere while claiming neutrality.
The attention-economy literature largely measures attention at the macro
level: time spent, clicks, or exposure.
A complementary micro-level question is
whether the listener is actually coupled to the broadcast at a given moment. Ze-
wail's (1999, 2000) pumpprobe experiments in femtochemistry provide a formal
analogy for this problem: a pump pulse launches a coherent state, and a delayed
probe measures it before dephasing destroys coherence.
The thesis borrows the
temporal structure, not the chemistry, to dene a time-resolved attentional gate
(Section 4.3.1). The analogy is useful precisely because it is falsiable: if the gate

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
24
does not improve retention, reputation, or rating predictions, it should be removed.
The attention-economy literature treats engagement metrics as choices about
what a platform rewards rather than neutral measures of social value. This moti-
vates comparing objective functions, but it does not establish that every increase
in engagement reduces epistemic quality. The present thesis explores that trade-o
in its specied simulation (Section 6.11), not as an already established universal
relationship.
2.9
The Velocity of Untruth
A major study of news diusion found faster, wider, and deeper propagation of
false than true stories in its Twitter dataset. Vosoughi et al. (2018) analysed the
diusion of true and false news on Twitter across roughly 126,000 cascades and
found that falsehoods were 70% more likely to be retweeted than true news, reached
1,500 people about six times sooner, and travelled deeper into the network, with
novelty and emotional charge as the plausible drivers. This evidence concerns the
diusion of classied news stories on Twitter; it does not directly estimate how a
radio listener judges a particular broadcaster. Brady et al. (2023) separately show
how observers can overperceive moral outrage and inate beliefs about intergroup
hostility. That nding concerns emotion perception, not a general law that reasoned
content always loses to outrage.
For EST, these studies motivate attention to amplication and perception as
distinct processes. A source-diversity statistic does not itself establish accuracy: a
diverse set can contain multiple inaccurate sources. Likewise, reducing concentration

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
25
does not necessarily improve a listener's ability to identify a false claim. The model
and its outcome measures must specify which of these changes they are intended to
produce.
2.10
The Parasocial Epistemic Bond
Horton and Wohl (1956) coined the term para-social interaction to describe the
one-sided intimacy audiences develop with media gures who address them directly.
The concept gives a vocabulary for relationships with mediated speakers. Spinelli
and Dann (2019) examine podcasting through interviews with producers and close
engagement with audio production and listening practices. Their account supports
studying intimacy and regularity as features of audio communication, but does not
provide an experimental estimate of the eect of a BRS display. Parasocial close-
ness can be a competing explanation for favourable ratings, not just a mechanism
conrming structural credibility.
The parasocial bond matters epistemically because trust is transferred from
person to proposition. A listener who trusts a host is more likely to accept the host's
claims with less scrutiny, which makes the bond a conduit for both veried knowledge
and misinformation. EST treats the parasocial bond as an interaction potential that
connects broadcaster reputation to content credibility, and the framework weights
endorsements by the credibility of the endorser precisely because parasocial trust is
powerful.

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
26
2.11
The Measurement of the Mind
The psychometric tradition demands that constructs be measured with explicit stan-
dards of reliability and validity. Cronbach (1951) supplied coecient alpha as an
internal-consistency coecient. The Standards for Educational and Psychological
Testing (American Educational Research Association [AERA] et al., 2014) address
evidence for score interpretations and uses, including consequences of measurement.
Kline (2023) explains conrmatory factor analysis as a way of evaluating a speci-
ed measurement structure. The t criteria examined by McNeish and Wolf (2023)
depend on model characteristics and should not be treated as universal passfail
rules independent of model and data.
Measurement invariance, the requirement
that a scale measure the same construct across groups, is operationalised through
congural, metric, and scalar models (Putnick & Bornstein, 2016). Boateng et al.
(2018) distinguish content development from empirical scale evaluation, a distinction
needed when expert judgments are not archived.
EST-P3 elevates these standards to a design principle: any metric that gov-
erns access, visibility, or reputation on an epistemic platform is a consequential
metric and must satisfy psychometric standards proportionate to its consequence.
The Broadcaster Reputation Score (BRS) is therefore specied in this thesis with an
explicit measurement model, reliability targets, and a proposed uncertainty display.
The questionnaire results in Chapter 6 assess internal consistency and factor t;
they do not establish calibration of broadcaster-specic algorithmic intervals.

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
27
2.12
The Student as Epistemic Agent
University students are relevant to this thesis as an audience engaged in formal
study and potentially in campus media production, not as an inherently homo-
geneous or media-literate population. Ashley (2020) situates news literacy in its
democratic and institutional context. This conceptual argument does not establish
that university attendance itself produces critical evaluation or validate a particular
student-rating algorithm. Vraga and Tully (2021) used a nationally representative
survey to examine news literacy, social media behaviors, and skepticism. Greater lit-
eracy and valuing literacy were associated with more skepticism about information
quality; seeing and posting news were not themselves associated with skepticism.
This is observational evidence, not a test of a literacy intervention or of an eect
of LOKLOK's design. Mihailidis (2019) argues that civic media literacy involves
social practices of connection as well as individual skills. These studies motivate
examining both individual capacities and opportunities for participation. They do
not establish that a particular interface causes better appraisal or production; that
relationship is a testable commitment of EST-P4 in the present framework.
The student-in-ride setting studied in this thesis is a concrete case: students
evaluate radio broadcasts during a bounded, compressed attention window. The
records can inform how listening context and perceived platform features relate to
audience evaluations. The survey does not separately randomise reputation cues,
source diversity, or reection prompts, so it cannot establish that those features
dominate content, familiarity, or context.

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
28
2.12.1
From Broadcast Evaluation to Student Competence
A student-development claim requires more than a satisfaction item. Koc and Barut
(2016) provide an instrument specically concerned with university students' new-
media competence, while the use of NMLS in Yavuzalp et al. (2021) provides further
context for its measurement structure. These sources support selecting an external
measure rather than constructing a Student Rating score by combining stars and
engagement. They do not establish the impact of LOKLOK or validate an Egyptian
translation.
This distinction is theoretically consequential. A platform can improve listen-
ers' evaluations without improving their critical production, and a more competent
listener may become less generous in rating weak content.
The thesis therefore
separates its existing audience measures from the competence prole and task ev-
idence specied in Section 3.7. The instrument is a measurement resource, not a
rival theory replacing EST; architecture remains the explanatory proposal whose
consequences the design tests.
2.13
Critical Synthesis and Competing Explanations
This is a theory-oriented narrative review, not a systematic review with a claim
to exhaustive retrieval. Its six dimensions operate at dierent levels: institutional
structures, platform rules, message diusion, relationships with speakers, measure-
ment, and educational practice.
Integration requires specifying how these levels
connect rather than assuming that evidence at one level automatically veries a
claim at another.

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
29
2.13.1
Source, Message, and Audience Evaluation
Appelman and Sundar (2016) distinguish message credibility from judgments about
a source or medium and develop a news-message credibility scale. This is useful for
EST because it identies a measurement boundary: perceived rigor of a broadcaster,
condence in a message, and overall satisfaction are not automatically the same
construct. Their scale-development results do not validate the dierently worded
PB items used here. Validation belongs to a specied instrument, population, and
interpretation.
Sundar (2020) develops a framework for the psychology of humanAI inter-
action, including how machine agency is encountered through interfaces. Applied
to this thesis, a high BRS could act as a cue rather than as evidence that a listener
checked the content. EST-P1 must therefore compete with an alternative explana-
tion: a visible reputation score changes the rating without changing either content
quality or the listener's ability to recognise accurate information. A eld design
should measure these outcomes separately.
2.13.2
Research Design and Transferability
Vosoughi et al. (2018) analyse large-scale diusion traces, whereas Bail et al. (2018)
use an intervention involving exposure to opposing political views. These approaches
answer dierent questions. Diusion patterns do not by themselves identify an ar-
chitectural treatment eect; an intervention in a particular political and platform
context does not determine its eect in Egyptian social radio. Producer-centred ac-
counts such as Spinelli and Dann (2019) oer interpretive depth but not comparable

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
30
eect estimates. These sources are complementary, not interchangeable replications
of EST.
The present ride-context survey adds a specic audience setting, but its small
convenience sample cannot establish national or cross-platform eects. The research
gap is therefore a need to connect architectural proposals with well-dened audience
measures and direct tests, not a claim that earlier communication scholarship ne-
glected audiences, power, or credibility.
2.13.3
Measurement and Rival Explanations
McNeish (2018) cautions against treating alpha as proof of a single dimension. Pod-
sako et al. (2024) review method-related sources of covariance in behavioural re-
search. These concerns are directly relevant when the same respondents rate several
favourable attributes during one questionnaire. A positive correlation pattern can
arise from shared response processes, overlapping content, or prior liking, as well
as from the proposed construct. The high SVPB and IQPB correlations in this
study must be read alongside its factor-model t rather than used to bypass that
evidence.
2.14
LLM Agents as a Computational Extension, Not Sub-
stitute Participants
Sundar (2020) distinguishes the symbolic and enabling eects of machine agency
on human experience. This is relevant to LOKLOK because an interface can both
oer an action and signal authority. It also creates a distinction for the extension:

an LLM producing a plausible explanation of trust is not the same as a human
experiencing a voice, interface, or journey.
Park et al.
(2023) demonstrate an agent architecture using memory, re-
ection, and planning to generate interactions in a sandbox environment. This is
a useful engineering precedent for persistent listeners and creators, not evidence
that emergent interactions reproduce Egyptian student behavior.
Park et al.'s
(2024) interview-grounded study simulates 1,052 individuals and evaluates responses
against human measures. It motivates richer anchoring than a short demographic
label. The cited version is a preprint, and its interview corpus and benchmarks dier
substantially from the present short, researcher-recorded ride accounts.
Argyle et al. (2023) examine conditioned language-model samples using U.S.
survey data. Aher et al. (2023) reproduce selected experimental patterns but also
identify systematic distortions, illustrating why successful examples cannot certify
a general human simulator. Dillion et al. (2023) likewise outline conditions and
caveats rather than an unrestricted replacement of participants. These studies sup-

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
32
port the extension as a testable modelling strategy, not as a way to enlarge the
human sample without recruitment.
The critical counterpoint is Bisbee et al. (2024): synthetic survey means can
look plausible while variation, regression relationships, and reproducibility remain
problematic. Accordingly, the LOKLOK extension must compare distributions and
behavior, not merely average PB; vary prompts and model versions; and preserve
unsuccessful runs. Descriptive plausibility, individual prediction, network dynamics,
and platform intervention eects are dierent evaluation targets. None follows from
a model agreeing with a favourable quotation.
2.14.1
Implication for the Present Research Programme
The empirical mixed-methods analysis establishes what the supplied students' rat-
ings and recorded accounts contain. The historical calibrated model explores speci-
ed rules. The new LLM extension will test whether evidence-grounded agents in-
teracting with actual LOKLOK software can produce useful, bounded predictions.
Qualitative themes guide which mechanisms to observe, while new, withheld human
outcomes are required if human predictive delity is claimed. This connects quali-
tative understanding to computation without treating students as xed stereotypes
or synthetic responses as new human evidence.
2.15
Synthesis and Implications for the Study
The six dimensions identify complementary concerns: institutional selection, com-
petition for attention, patterns of misinformation diusion, parasocial relationships,

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
33
measurement quality, and educational opportunity. They are not six universal laws.
Trust need not be exclusively parasocial, falsehood need not always spread faster,
and participation need not entail learning. Their integration in EST is valuable
only if the proposed connections retain these boundaries and generate discriminat-
ing tests.

The review supports seven conclusions. First, internet radio, podcasting, and
social media radio overlap without being identical. Second, platform inuence must
be located in production, discovery, circulation, or governance rather than assigned
to an unspecied algorithm. Third, audience judgments, content accuracy, sharing,
and learning require distinct measures. Fourth, Egyptian audience research provides
a relevant context but not a substitute for evidence about this specic sample. Fifth,
neither high alpha nor a successful model run establishes the validity of the entire
theory. Sixth, qualitative accounts should elaborate and challenge ratings rather
than serve as decorative conrmation.
Seventh, evidence-grounded LLM agents
remain models requiring held-out evaluation, not substitutes for additional human

CHAPTER 2. CRITICAL REVIEW OF SIX EPISTEMIC DIMENSIONS OF SOCIAL
MEDIA AUDIO
34
participants. These conclusions motivate both the mixed-methods analysis and the
explicit separation of the planned platform extension.

EST is the researcher's proposed synthesis of these problems. Its value rests
on explicit mechanisms and tests that could challenge them, not on declaring pre-
vious communication theories obsolete. Chapter 3 develops the propositions; sub-
sequent chapters distinguish their implementation, observed audience associations,
and conditional model predictions.
Chapter summary. The review nds a fragmented literature: strong evi-
dence on attention, misinformation, and parasocial trust, but weaker evidence
on how architecture and measurement rules jointly shape student evaluation. It
justies an exploratory design study rather than a causal test, and it identies
the constructs that must be measured: credibility, diversity, echo, perceived
benet, and competence.
